rulegroup.name: An ATDD Technical Name is not a verb

rule.name: train is a Technical Name, not a verb
rule.message: "train" is an ATDD Technical Name — the ordered sequence of wagons. Do not use it as a verb. Rewrite the sentence around the noun.
rule.example: We train the runner on the new wagons.
The train runs the wagons in sequence.

rule.name: contract is a Technical Name, not a verb
rule.message: "contract" is an ATDD Technical Name — the versioned interface between a workspace provider and an implementation. Do not use it as a verb.
rule.example: The scan roots contract to one directory.
The implementation declares the provider contract.

rule.name: feature is a Technical Name, not a verb
rule.message: "feature" is an ATDD Technical Name — a URN-addressed unit of capability. Do not use it as a verb.
rule.example: The reports feature a summary line.
The WMBT binds to one feature.

rule.name: gate is a Technical Name, not a verb
rule.message: "gate" is an ATDD Technical Name — the stage declaration that decides when an implementation runs. Write "the gate blocks" or "the gate runs", not "we gate".
rule.example: We gate the merge on this rule.
The CI gate blocks the merge on this rule.

rule.name: scope is a Technical Name, not a verb
rule.message: "scope" is an ATDD Technical Name — the selector set that binds a rule to the files it inspects. Do not use it as a verb.
rule.example: We scope the rule to python/.
The scope binds the rule to python/.

rule.name: coach is a persona name, not a verb
rule.message: "coach" is the ATDD persona that owns the lifecycle. Do not use it as a verb.
rule.example: The gate coaches the author.
The coach persona owns the lifecycle.

rule.name: interlocking is a Technical Name
rule.message: "interlocking" is an ATDD Technical Name — the route-control layer that selects a train. Do not use it as a present participle.
rule.example: The routes are interlocking at run time.
The interlocking selects the train.

rule.name: artifact is spelled with an i
rule.message: ATDD spells this term "artifact". "artefact" is not in the approved word list.
rule.example: The authored artefact is governed.
The authored artifact is governed.

rule.name: realize is spelled with a z
rule.message: ATDD spells the Technical Verb "realize" and its noun "realization" with a z, to match `realizes_convention` in every implementation manifest.
rule.example: The detector realises the convention.
The detector realizes the convention.

rule.name: convention node is two words
rule.message: Write the Technical Name as two words: "convention node".
rule.example: The convention-node carries one rule id.
The convention node carries one rule id.

rule.name: station master is two words
rule.message: Write the Technical Name as two words: "station master".
rule.example: The stationmaster selects the route.
The station master selects the route.

rule.name: workspace is one word
rule.message: Write the Technical Name as one word: "workspace".
rule.example: The implementation targets a work space.
The implementation targets a workspace.

rule.name: runtime is one word as a noun
rule.message: As a Technical Name, write "runtime" as one word. Two words is the adverbial "at run time".
rule.example: The provider owns the run time.
The provider owns the runtime.

rule.name: cargo is a mass noun
rule.message: "cargo" is the artifact data plane and is a mass noun. Write "cargo", not a plural.
rule.example: The runner carries two cargos.
The runner carries the cargo between wagons.

rule.name: suppress-and-clean is hyphenated
rule.message: The disposition value is written "suppress-and-clean", with hyphens, exactly as the convention nodes declare it.
rule.example: The rule is suppress and clean.
The rule is suppress-and-clean.

rule.name: WMBT is written in capital letters
rule.message: "WMBT" ("What Must Be True") is an abbreviation. Write it in capital letters; write the plural as "WMBTs".
rule.example: The wagon declares one wmbt.
The wagon declares one WMBT.

rule.name: URN is written in capital letters
rule.message: "URN" is an abbreviation. Write it in capital letters; write the plural as "URNs".
rule.example: The artifact carries one urn.
The artifact carries one URN.

rule.name: ATDD is written in capital letters
rule.message: "ATDD" is written in capital letters in prose. The lowercase form `atdd` is the command and the package namespace, which are identifiers, not prose.
rule.example: The atdd substrate governs the artifact.
The ATDD substrate governs the artifact.

rule.name: YAML, JSON, XML, HTTP and AST are written in capital letters
rule.message: Write this abbreviation in capital letters: YAML, JSON, XML, HTTP, AST.
rule.example: The manifest is a yaml file.
The manifest is a YAML file.

rule.name: A product name keeps its vendor spelling
rule.message: Write the product name in its vendor spelling: TypeScript, JavaScript, GitHub, LanguageTool, TechScribe, FastAPI, SonarQube.
rule.example: The detector reads Typescript source.
The detector reads TypeScript source.

rule.name: A runtime class name keeps its PascalCase
rule.message: Write the runtime Technical Name in PascalCase: TrainRunner, InterlockingRunner, TrainResult, InterlockingResolution.
rule.example: The consumer ships an Interlockingrunner.
The consumer ships an InterlockingRunner.
